June 28, 1916.

REPORT ON Kidnapping of Daung Chi Sing.

Made by D. S. Givens. Forwarded by

Sir,
Regarding the kidnapping of Daung Chi Sing, I am herewith
attaching the statements of two more men. These throw further
light on how the kidnapping was affected. Inquiries are being
made regarding the suspects, and they will be arrested when
located.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
Detective Sergeant.

Chief Detective Inspector.

June 24th 1916.

My name is Liang Tih Vung ( 梁秩文 ), I reside at NO.146
Ching Yuin Li ( 青雲里 ), Tiendong Road, I am a Cantonese, and am
employed as a shipping broker in Tong Hing Yuen ( 東興源 ) Co.
at NO 63 Kiangse Road. Daung Chi Sing ( 唐继星 ) was a friend
of mine, and his letters used to be addressed to my care. About
3 p.m. 4th March 1916, when I went to my office, I found a letter
there for Daung. The same evening I took to Lieu Hwe Ding ( 刘辉亭 )
and requested him to deliver it. The address on letters
sent to me for Daung Chi Sing used to bear one of his private
names which were Bang Seu Koong ( 彭銳公 ) and Kau Sz San ( 高如山 ).
The letter in question was addresed to the first of these names.

1916年6月24日。

本人名叫梁秩文（Liang Tih Vung），住天潼路青雲里146號，籍貫廣東，在江西路63號東興源（Tong Hing Yuen）公司擔任船務經紀人。唐繼星（Daung Chi Sing）是我的朋友，他的信件通常寄由我轉交。1916年3月4日下午3點左右，當我去辦公室時，發現那裡有一封給唐繼星的信。當天晚上，我將信交給劉輝亭（Lieu Hwe Ding），請他代為送達。寄給我轉交唐繼星的信件上，通常寫有他的別名之一，即彭銳公（Bang Seu Koong）和高如山（Kau Sz San）。涉案這封信是寫給前一個名字的。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE. No....................
CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION DEPARTMENT. Date....................
STATEMENT.
Shanghai, June 23, 1916.
Statement of Lieu Kwe Ding (劉輝亭).
My name is Lieu Kwe Ding (劉輝亭). I am a native of Canton
and reside at No. 381 West Kashing Road. I was formerly a
military officer, and am now a doctor.
About 8 p.m. 4th March, 1916. a friend named Liang Dih Vang,梁狄文
came to my house and gave me a letter, which he requested me to
take to one Daung Chi Sing, who was our mutual friend. I used
to visit Daung Chi Sing's house which was in Frenchtown frequently,
and I took the letter to him the following morning at 8 o'clock.
When Daung Chi Sing had read the letter, he told me that it was
written by one Daung Nyoh Hyien (唐玉軒 ), his nephew residing
in Boone Road, and that it was an invitation to Daung Chi Sing
to visit Daung Nyoh Hyien. Daung Chi Sing, who was a rebel and
afraid of Government agents, said that he did not wish to visit
his nephew as several secret detectives lived in the vicinity of
the latter's house. Daung Chi Sing then gave me a letter of
introduction, and requested me to visit his nephew's house, and
ascertain what he wanted, and I did so. When Daung Hyoh Hyien had
read his uncle's letter, he said that the matter about which he
wished to speak with his uncle was very private, and it was
imperative that he should see him personally. I returned to Daung
Chi Sing's house, and told him what had occurred and he said he
would go that evening to see his nephew. On the morning of March
7th, I went to Daung Chi Sing's house, where his wife told me that
he had left for his nephew's home the previous evening, and had
failed to return. I then went to the nephew's house, and his
wife told me that he was out. I asked her if Daung Chi Sing had
been to her house the previous evening, and she replied in the
negative. I went back and reported to Mrs. Daung Chi Sing what
had taken place. The latter and I went back to Daung Nyoh Hyien's

上海，1916年6月23日。
劉輝亭（Lieu Kwe Ding）的供詞。
本人名叫劉輝亭（Lieu Kwe Ding）。我是廣東人，住西嘉興路381號。我曾是軍官，現在是一名醫生。
1916年3月4日晚上8點左右，一位名叫梁狄文（Liang Dih Vang）的朋友來到我家，給了我一封信，請求我送給我們共同的朋友唐繼星。我以前經常去唐繼星位於法租界的家，第二天早上8點，我把信送給了他。唐繼星讀完信後告訴我，信是他的侄子唐玉軒（Daung Nyoh Hyien）寫的，他住在布恩路（Boone Road），信是邀請唐繼星去拜訪他。唐繼星是一名反叛分子，害怕政府人員，他說他不想去拜訪他的侄子，因為後者住所附近住著幾名秘密偵探。隨後，唐繼星給了我一封介紹信，請求我去他侄子家，查明他有什麼事，我便照辦了。唐玉軒（Daung Hyoh Hyien）讀完叔叔的信後說，他想與叔叔談的事情非常私密，必須親自見面。我回到唐繼星家，告訴他發生的情況，他說他當天晚上會去看望他的侄子。3月7日早上，我去了唐繼星家，他的妻子告訴我，他前一天晚上已經前往侄子家，至今未歸。於是我去到侄子家，他的妻子告訴我他出去了。我问她唐繼星前一天晚上是否來過她家，她回答沒有。我回去向唐繼星夫人報告了所發生的一切。她和我也回到了唐玉軒（Daung Nyoh Hyien）的

June 19th, 1916.

REPORT ON Kidnapping of Daung Chi Sing.

Made by D. S. Givens. Forwarded by

Sir,
Regarding the kidnapping of Daung Chi Sing, I am attaching
a statement by one Daung Bah ( 唐枝 ), a brother of the
kidnapped man to whom the body was handed in Peking, and a
a document issued by the Peking Military Court ordering
the removal of the body. A warrant has been applied for in
accordance with the instructions of the Captain-Superintendent.
It is now in this office.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D. S. Givens
Detective Sergeant.

Chief Detective Inspector.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE. Del....................................
CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION DEPARTMENT.
STATEMENT.
June 19th, 1916.

Daung Bah alias Foh Sz. 唐拔即法思

My name is Daung Bah, but I am also known as Foh Sz. I am thirty-five years old, and a native of Canton. I reside at No. 83 San Tu Lee alleyway near the West Gate. I am a clerk in the China Merchants Steam Navigation Co.

On 7th March 1916 I went to see my brother Daung Chi Sing, and was informed by his wife that he had not returned home the previous night. On the same day I got news that my brother was in custody in a Chinese police station, and I reported the matter to the French Police. A week later I saw in the newspapers that Daung Chi Sing had been sent to Peking, and three or four days later a report appeared in the newspaper that he had been shot in the capital. Apart from the statement in the newspapers, there were several rumours regarding the fate of my brother. Some confirmed the fatal news in the press, while others were to the effect that he was still alive. When Yuan Shih Kai announced that he had abandoned his monarchical programme I decided to risk a visit to the capital and find out definitely what had become of my brother. I arrived in Peking on or about 12th April. After six days inquiries, I learned that my brother had been shot at a place called Nan Yen (南苑) five miles from the South Gate of Peking. I then went to see a military officer named Tsu Zau Ziang (周兆祥) who was in charge of the coffins containing rebel corpses. He confirmed the news of my brother's execution, but said he had no power to hand over the corpse. On his advice I approached a General named Lai Tseng Chun (雷震春), a friend named Daung Zee Li (唐在禮), acting as intermediang. The following day Daung gave me a permit bearing the chop of the Military Court authorising me to take away the body. Eight days later the coffin containing the body of Daung Chi Sing was handed

1916年6月19日。

唐拔（Daung Bah），又名法思（Foh Sz）。

本人名叫唐拔，但也稱為法思。我今年三十五歲，廣東人。我住西門附近的三圖里弄83號。我是招商局輪船公司的職員。

1916年3月7日，我去看望我的哥哥唐繼星，從他妻子那裡得知他前一晚沒有回家。當天，我得到消息說我的哥哥被關押在中國警察局，我便向法國警察報告了此事。一週後，我在報紙上看到唐繼星已被送往北京，三四天後，報紙上又出現報道稱他在京城被槍決。除了報紙上的聲明外，關於我哥哥的命運還有各種謠言。有些證實了報上的死訊，而另一些則稱他仍然活著。當袁世凱宣佈放棄帝制計劃時，我決定冒險前往京城，徹底查清我哥哥的下落。我於4月12日左右抵達北京。經過六天的查詢，我得知我哥哥在北京南門五英里處的南苑（Nan Yen）被槍決。隨後我去見了一位負責裝有反叛者屍體棺材的軍官周兆祥（Tsu Zau Ziang）。他確認了我哥哥被處決的消息，但說他無權移交屍體。在他的建議下，我通過一位名叫唐在禮（Daung Zee Li）的朋友作為中間人，接觸了一位名叫雷震春（Lai Tseng Chun）的將軍。第二天，唐在禮給了我一張蓋有軍事法庭印章的許可證，授權我帶走屍體。八天後，裝有唐繼星屍體的棺材被移交

Shanghai Municipal Council.
June 7th 1916

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL）
POLICE FORCE,
(DETECTIVE BRANCH.)

Sir,
I have been informed that Yang Toheng 楊晟 the
Special Envoy for Foreign Affairs, is implicated in
the case wherein one Tang Chi Sung 唐純星 a resident
of the French Concession was kidnapped from the
International Settlement on March 6th 1916.
The kidnapping was arranged and carried out through
the treachery of a relative. A reward of $40,000
was offered for his arrest but only $5000 of this
has been paid.
Tang Chi Sung 唐純星 was immediately removed from
the place where he was seized to the Railway Station
and taken to the north by train. He was shot at
Peking. His body is now at Tientsin. It will be
handed over to his relatives.
Yang Toheng 楊晟 at once sent off a telegram
to Peking announcing the capture but he concealed
the information from the Military Governor at the time
hoping to gain the credit of the business entirely
to himself.

Your Obedient Servant,
William Armstrong
Chief Detective Inspector.

C.O.I.
Having confirmed the fact
that Tang was taken to
Peking there seems to have
been a fairly strong
case of kidnapping. If
Warrant should be applied for
now, whether the file to
Captain Superintendent of Police.
be for representations to be made to
the Council.

8/15.
AM

1916年6月7日

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL）
警務處，
（偵緝科。）

先生，
據悉，外交特派員楊晟（Yang Toheng）牽涉進一起案件，該案中，法租界居民唐純星（Tang Chi Sung）於1916年3月6日在公共租界被綁架。
綁架是通過一名親屬的背叛策劃並實施的。曾懸賞40,000美元捉拿兇手，但僅支付了其中的5,000美元。
唐純星（Tang Chi Sung）在被抓獲後立即從被抓地點被帶往火車站，並乘火車北上。他在北京被槍決。他的遺體現在天津。將移交給其親屬。
楊晟（Yang Toheng）隨即發出一封電報到北京宣佈抓獲消息，但他當時向督軍隱瞞了這一信息，希望將此事的功勞完全歸於自己。

您忠實的僕人，
William Armstrong
首席探長。

C.O.I.
既然已確認唐氏
被帶往北京的事實，
似乎存在相當有力的
綁架證據。如果
現在申請逮捕令，
是否應將檔案提交
給警察總巡長，
以便向董事會提出交涉。

8/15.
AM
9/6

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION DEPARTMENT.
STATEMENT.

Shanghai, July 3, 1916.

My name is Moh Ling ( 莫倫 ). I am a native of Canton, aged
42. I am a Chinese cook by trade. I am unemployed now. I was
last employed in Yangtsepoo district, and left my position there
seven
about or eight years ago. Since then I have been a hawker in
the vicinity of Woosung Road. I reside at 283 Yoong Nyih Li
( 崇業里 ) Woosung Road. O.O.L. I was arrested for gambling by
the Chapei Police on or about 2nd March, 1916. I was confined
in the Chapei Central Station. After I had been four days in
gaol about 10 p.m. a Cantonese, whom I afterwards learned was
named Daung Chi Sing was brought to my cell. He told me that
two of his relations had invited him from his house in Frenchtown
to go to see a sister who was ill. On arriving at a place in
the neighbourhood of Range and Woosung Roads, he was set upon
by detectives who threatened him with revolvers, and took him
to the Chapei Central Station. I was released the following day.
Before leaving the cell, Daung Chi Sing gave me a chit addressed
to 381 West Woochang Road. I delivered the note to his wife.

The above statement was given by
In the presence of D. S.

供詞。

上海，1916年7月3日。

本人名叫莫倫（Moh Ling）。我是廣東人，42歲。職業是中國廚師。目前失業。我最後一次受僱是在楊樹浦區，大約七八年前離開了那裡的職位。此後，我一直在吳淞路附近做小販。我住吳淞路崇業里（Yoong Nyih Li）283號。O.O.L. 我於1916年3月2日左右因賭博被閘北警察逮捕。我被關押在閘北中央捕房。我在監獄裡待了四天後，大約晚上10點，一名廣東人被帶到我的牢房，後來我得知他名叫唐繼星。他告訴我，他的兩個親屬從他在法租界的家中邀請他去看望一位生病的妹妹。當到達吳淞路和蘭路（Range Road）附近的一個地方時，他遭到手持左輪手槍威脅的偵探襲擊，並被帶到閘北中央捕房。我第二天被釋放。在離開牢房之前，唐繼星給了我一張寫有西武昌路381號地址的紙條。我把紙條交給了他的妻子。

以上供詞由
在 D. S. 面前提供

My name is Daung Bah, but I am also known as Foh Sz. I am

On 7th March 1916 I went to see my brother Daung Chi Sing, 
and was informed by his wife that he had not returned home the 
previous night. On the same day I got news that my brother was 
in custody in a Chinese police station, and I reported the matted 
to the French Police. A week later I saw in the newspapers that 
Daung Chi Sing had been sent to Peking, and three or four days 
later a report appeared in the newspaper that he had been shot 


in the capital. Apart from the statement in the newspapers, there 


were several rumours regarding the fate of my brother. Some 
confirmed the fatal news in the press, while others were to the 
effect that he was still alive. When Yuan Shih Kai announced 
that he had abandoned his monarchical programme I decided to risk 
@ visit to the capital and find out definitely what had become of

I approached a General named Lai Tseng Chun ( & za ), a 
friend named Daung Zee Li ( /fé Bae )» acting as intermediang.
